name: Gigachad
blurb: A black-and-white photo of an absurdly chiselled man: the ultimate confident "chad"
title: Gigachad Meme: Meaning, Origin & Who the Man Is
description: Gigachad is a heavily edited black-and-white photo of a muscular man from Krista Sudmalis's Sleek'N'Tears project. 4chan named it "Gigachad" in October 2017.
answer: Gigachad is a black-and-white photo of a man with an absurdly sharp jaw, huge muscles and a calm stare, used to represent the most confident, attractive man imaginable: the ultimate "chad". The images come from the photographer Krista Sudmalis's art project Sleek'N'Tears, where they were heavily retouched; the man is known online as Ernest Khalimov. A 4chan post called him "Gigachad" in October 2017, and the meme exploded in early 2021 with the "Average Fan vs. Average Enjoyer" format.

body: The best-known Gigachad shots are moody, high-contrast black-and-white portraits: a man with a massive square jaw, sculpted cheekbones, slicked-back hair and a chest like a statue, often looking off to the side. The proportions are pushed by photo editing, which is part of why the pictures look almost unreal.
In memes he plays the calm, unbothered winner. "Chad" was already internet slang for a confident, attractive man; "giga" turns that up to the maximum.

head: Date
Event
rows: A Reddit user links the Sleek'N'Tears Instagram page; a day later a 4chan post calls the man "Gigachad".
The photo is posted to Reddit's r/Bossfight as "Gigachad, the destroyer of virgins" and spreads further.
The "Average Fan vs. Average Enjoyer" video pairs a crying Wojak fan with a stoic Gigachad; the template spreads immediately.
Gigachad's popularity spikes as the Fan vs. Enjoyer format goes viral.
The man behind the photos first acknowledges the memes on Instagram and says he likes them.

ul: Average Fan vs. Average Enjoyer: a whiny Wojak "fan" on the left, a calm Gigachad "enjoyer" on the right, who likes the same thing without drama.
Replying to an argument with just the Gigachad face and a short line like "Yes.", meaning "I'm confident and I don't care".
Gigachad as the "based" choice in jokes: "Gigachad move: replying to emails on time."
Video edits with dramatic music, where someone does something bold and their face turns into Gigachad.

body: Gigachad is still one of the go-to images for confidence and "winning" in meme formats, and it feeds into newer slang like sigma, mewing and mogging. Most people use it ironically. The photos belong to the Sleek'N'Tears project; who exactly is in them has never been fully confirmed in reliable sources, and the name Ernest Khalimov is how the account presents him.

faq.a: The photos show a real model, but they were heavily edited for Krista Sudmalis's Sleek'N'Tears project. Online he is known as Ernest Khalimov.
Internet slang for a confident, attractive, successful man. "Gigachad" is the extreme version.

faq.q: What is "Average Fan vs. Average Enjoyer"?
faq.a: A 2021 meme format comparing an anxious, complaining fan (a Wojak) with a calm Gigachad who simply enjoys the same thing.
